sanskrit: yebhiḥ pāśair abhidadhāsi druhvaṇaḥ samāmino anṛtaṃ ye samāmire | tāṃs te vi ṣyāmy āyuṣe balāya- -anamīvaṃ pitum addhi prasūtaḥ ||
english: Those bonds with which you bind the treacherous ones, those who have joined together in falsehood — those I loosen from you, for life and strength. Eat food free from disease, you who are born forth.

sanskrit: anāgā babhro ayam astu vīro druhaḥ pāśebhyaḥ pari pāhy enam | rājan pravidvān pra mumugdhi pāśān yasmai carāmi haviṣā ghṛtena ||
english: O tawny one (Varuṇa), may this hero be free from guilt; guard him from the bonds of treachery. O king, all-knowing, release the bonds of him for whom I perform rites with oblation and ghee.

sanskrit: kaśyapa indrāya haviṣā cacāra haritvatīṣu maghavā maghone | paspāra viśvā bhuvanasya gopā antarikṣasya mahato vimāne ||
english: Kaśyapa moved with oblation toward Indra among the golden-hued ones; the bountiful lord gave to the bountiful. The guardian of all being traversed the great expanse of the vast atmosphere.

sanskrit: apūpaṃ nābhilaṃ te ghṛtaścutaṃ nadīnāṃ pade suśrutaṃ juhomi | pravidvān rājan pra mumugdhi pāśān anyasya patnī vidhavā yathāsat ||
english: The round cake, the navel-shaped one, dripping with ghee, well-renowned at the ford of the rivers — this I offer to you. O knowing king, release the bonds, lest another man's wife become a widow.

sanskrit: anātureṇa varuṇaḥ pathemaṃ svastibhir ati durgāṇi neṣat | tam aśvinā pratigṛhyā svastaye doṣā enam uṣase saṃ pra yacchāt ||
english: May Varuṇa lead him unharmed along this path, conducting him past all difficulties with blessings. Receiving him, may the Aśvins hand him over, for well-being, from dusk to dawn.

sanskrit: ye piśācā imāṃ vittim ākūtiṃ mohayanti naḥ | teṣāṃ tvam agne nāśaya varcaś cittam atho prajām ||
english: Those Piśācas who befuddle our understanding and intent — their brilliance, their mind, and their offspring: destroy these, O Agni.

sanskrit: nāśayāgne piśācānāṃ varcaś cittam atho prajām | athāśāṃ mahyaṃ rādhaya yathāhaṃ kāmaye tathā ||
english: Destroy, O Agni, the brilliance, mind, and offspring of the Piśācas; and then fulfil my desire according to how I wish it.

sanskrit: āśāṃ mahyaṃ rādhayitvā- -indriyeṇa yathāmṛtām | tvam agne kravyādaḥ sarvān piśācām̐ arciṣā daha ||
english: Having fulfilled my desire with vital power as though immortal, you, O Agni, flesh-consuming one, burn all the Piśācas with your flame.

sanskrit: prati daha yātudhānān mūradevān vicarṣaṇe | ye no durasyā dveṣeṇa- -athāśāṃ mohayanti naḥ ||
english: Burn back the sorcerers, the foolish pseudo-gods, O all-seeing one — those who, with hatred seek to harm us and confound our desire.

sanskrit: ye naḥ paśuṣu dipsanty āśāyāṃ puruṣeṣu ca | tāṃs tvaṃ sahasrākṣeśānaḥ piśācām̐ arciṣā daha ||
english: Those who seek to harm us in our cattle and in our desires and in our people — them, O thousand-eyed lord, burn those Piśācas with your flame.

sanskrit: sahasvedaṃ sahamāne atho devi sarasvati | athedam aśvinā lakṣma rohitaṃ kṛṇutaṃ yuvam ||
english: Together with these, O all-overcoming one, and also O goddess Sarasvatī — and this: O you two Aśvins, make this mark red.

sanskrit: āsurasya mukhasyāgne lakṣmamukhaṃ nāmāsi | meto jyāyo bhūr ita it kanīyo 'so naśyetaḥ paro mā tvā hiṃsiṣam ||
english: O Agni, you are called the mark-face of the Āsura's face. Become greater from here, become smaller from there; depart, be gone — may the far one not injure you.

sanskrit: yāsāṃ pitā parjanyo bhūmir mātā babhūva | hvayāmi sarvā oṣadhīr gojātāḥ somajinvatāḥ ||
english: Those whose father is Parjanya and whose mother has become the Earth — I summon all those plants, the cow-born ones, those quickened by Soma.

sanskrit: idaṃ saptaprakhe tvaṃ kilāsaṃ nāśayā tvacaḥ | niṣkṛtir nāma vā asi sedaṃ niṣ kṛdhi bhadrayā ||
english: O seven-branched one, destroy this kilāsa-blemish from the skin. Indeed you are named Niṣkṛti — cure this with your auspiciousness.

sanskrit: niṣkṛtir nāma te mātā niṣkṛtir nāma te pitā | uto tvam asi niṣkṛtiḥ sedaṃ niṣ kṛdhi bhadrayā ||
english: Niṣkṛti is the name of your mother, Niṣkṛti is the name of your father; and you yourself are Niṣkṛti — cure this with your auspiciousness.
